review_notes: I read the whole target file (lines 1–1272) and the definitions it depends on: poitouKernel/poitouTransform/poitouTransformIntegrand (PoitouTransform.lean), regularizedScaledTartar (RegularizedTartar.lean), regularizedScaledTartarDerivative and its bound (TartarDerivativeBounds.lean), Tartar.weight/amplitude/testFunction (TestFunction/Basic.lean, TestFunction/Fourier.lean), fan-out of the Fourier identities (RegularizedTartarTransform.lean), and downstream users (RegularizedPrimePowerSeriesIntegral.lean, PoitouEstimate.lean, RegularizedPoitouContourLimit.lean). I re-derived the statements algebraically: the derivative formulas for poitouKernelDerivative/poitouKernelSecondDerivative and for regularizedScaledTartarSecondDerivative, the constants in abs_poitouKernelDerivative_le (|f'|+|f|/2), abs_poitouKernelSecondDerivative_le (|f''|+|f'|+3|f|/4), abs_regularizedScaledTartarSecondDerivative_le (8δ|y|B'|x|), and the quadratic majorants in norm_poitouVerticalProfile{Derivative,SecondDerivative}_regularized_le all match. I checked that the bounds are not vacuous: Tartar.weight = max (1-x^2) 0 has ∫t^2 w = 2/5 and tartarAmplitudeDerivativeBound = 3/8 > 0, so bounds such as abs_tartarAmplitudeSecondDerivative_le/abs_tartarTestFunctionSecondDerivative_le have nonzero constants, and the amplitude second-derivative bound is attained at x = 0 (amplitude''(0) = -1/5 = -(3/4)∫t^2w). No statement in the first five sections has an inconsistent hypothesis set or a trivializing definition. The one issue I found is recorded below: the Poitou/Fourier identification theorem has no integrability/positivity hypothesis, so for δ < 0 both sides are the default (junk) value 0. I could not compile anything; the proposed repair is a statement change that would require passing the new hypothesis at the existing call sites (all of which already have 0 < δ in context, e.g. line 1225 and RegularizedPrimePowerSeriesIntegral.lean:143).

findings.excerpt:
theorem poitouTransform_regularizedScaledTartar_eq_fourier
    (y δ σ t : ℝ) :
    poitouTransform (regularizedScaledTartar y δ) (σ + t * I) =
      𝓕 (regularizedPoitouVerticalProfile y δ σ)
        (-t / (2 * Real.pi)) := by
findings.problem: The statement quantifies over every real δ, but the equation is vacuous on the whole δ < 0 part of its domain. Explicitly, take y = 1, δ = -1, σ = 1/2, t = 0. Since regularizedScaledTartar 1 (-1) x = Tartar.testFunction x * Real.exp (x^2), and Tartar.testFunction x = Tartar.amplitude x ^ 2 with Tartar.amplitude x = 3 * (Real.sin x - x * Real.cos x) / x^3 for x ≠ 0, the profile is x ↦ Tartar.testFunction x * Real.exp (x^2) / Real.cosh (x/2), which is unbounded along any sequence with |cos x| bounded away from 0; hence regularizedPoitouVerticalProfile 1 (-1) (1/2) is not integrable. Because poitouTransform is defined as a Bochner integral, and Real.fourier_real_eq_integral_exp_smul exhibits 𝓕 as a Bochner integral as well, both sides are the default value 0 for non-integrable inputs. So the theorem reduces to 0 = 0 for every δ < 0 (and also for δ = 0 with σ > 1), and it never records the condition under which the two displayed objects are genuine transforms. Every other lemma in this file that really needs the exponential decay carries hδ : 0 < δ (regularizedPoitouVerticalProfile_integrable at lines 499-501, fourier_poitouVerticalProfileDerivative_regularized at 556-557, sq_abs_mul_norm_poitouTransform_regularized_le at 1225-1226), so the missing hypothesis here is an inconsistency rather than a deliberate generalisation.
findings.proposed_change: Add the hypothesis {δ : ℝ} (hδ : 0 < δ) to poitouTransform_regularizedScaledTartar_eq_fourier (lines 506-510), or alternatively an explicit hypothesis Integrable (regularizedPoitouVerticalProfile y δ σ), so that the identity is only advertised where the Poitou transform and Fourier transform are real integrals; if the hypothesis-free formal identity is wanted for the proof, state it as a separate private/auxiliary lemma and expose the 0 < δ version. The existing call site at line 1252 (inside sq_abs_mul_norm_poitouTransform_regularized_le, which already has hδ) and the downstream rewrites in RegularizedPrimePowerSeriesIntegral.lean (lines 143, 181, 244) all have 0 < δ available, so they can pass the new hypothesis.
findings.benefit: Users then get the Fourier representation of the Poitou transform for exactly the parameter range in which the two sides are genuine integrals, and cannot apply a statement whose content is the junk equality 0 = 0. It also makes the hypothesis requirements of this file uniform with its integrability and Fourier-derivative lemmas.

noncomputable def poitouTransform (f : ℝ → ℝ) (s : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  ∫ x : ℝ, poitouTransformIntegrand f s x

noncomputable def regularizedScaledTartar
    (y δ x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  scaledTartarTestFunction y x * Real.exp (-δ * x ^ 2)

noncomputable def Tartar.amplitude (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  if x = 0 then 1 else 3 * (Real.sin x - x * Real.cos x) / x ^ 3
